utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Gotovina, et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Is the Markac Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that will be no protective measures, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From what I remember, there were no objections against the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can say that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. De Landri, your microphone was not activated, so earphones on, switch on the microphone and --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. Vurnek. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration of which the text will now be handed out to you by Madam Usher. I would like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Vurnek. Mr. Vurnek, you'll first be examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic. Mr. Kuzmanovic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm just going to move over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: [In English] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please state your name for the record, your full name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragutin Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And what is your current function as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm chief of the Koprivnica-Krizevci police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we please have 65 ter 3D00890 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: While that's coming up on the screen, Mr. Vurnek, do you recall giving a statement to the members of the Markac Defence in May of this year?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to the last page of the Croatian version, please, of both versions, actually. On the last page of the Croatian version, is your signature there, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall being interviewed in May 2009 - excuse me - by members of the Markac Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The statement was signed and on the first date of the -- or on the first page of the statement, it's dated 18th of May of 2009. Does that recall -- do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I remember the conversation we had in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you had a chance before coming to testify to review the statement that is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that statement accurately reflect what you told members of the Markac Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time that you gave this statement, did you give it to the best of your knowledge and in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If I asked you the same questions today in court that you were asked prior to signing the witness statement that's on the screen, would you provide the same answers today in court as you did to the questions that were posed to you during the course of the interview that led to the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the same answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this statement be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D1895. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1895 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, may I read a summary of the witnesses testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During Operation Storm, Mr. Vurnek held a position of assistant commander of the special police unit of the Sisak-Moslavina police administration. Mr. Vurnek arrived with his unit on Mount Velebit a few days before Operation Storm commenced. On the 3rd of August, all commanders attended a meeting in Stari Grad where they received their orders. The commanders were also instructed to adhere to international law of war, and the proper treatment of civilians and property was stressed. The information acquired during this meeting was passed on to Mr. Vurnek and his unit. Mr. Vurnek stated that according to instructions any civilians found were to be handed over to special police staff who then organised their transfer to regular or civilian police. On August 4th, Mr. Vurnek's unit was to break through the front line in the Crni Vrh area and reach the Ruka-Papuca road. There they came in contact with the enemy and heavy combat. On August 5th the unit entered Gracac at about 1400 hours. On August 6th they rested and prepared for further combat activity. While in Gracac his unit was not involved in combat activities, as the enemy had already withdrawn. He did not witness any damage in Gracac town, nor did he observe any members of the special police destroying or stealing property. On August 7, together with other special police units, he was relocated to Bruvno. After the liberation of Mazin, his unit moved forward to Dobroselo. On the way to Dobroselo, they observed a mixed convoy of military and civilian vehicles driving in the direction of Srb, Martin Brod, but they did not engage in any combat activities. His unit continued to advance towards Gornji Lapac which was unpopulated and undamaged. Later that day his unit received an order to advance toward Kulen Vakuf and reached Kulen Vakuf without enemy contact. His unit then handed their positions to the Croatian army on the 8th or 9th of August, and they subsequently returned to their base in Kutina. His unit did not require after the Gracac operation the use of any artillery support. That's the statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, can you please tell the Trial Chamber about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I graduated from the faculty of physical education, and from the police academy, I became a graduate criminologist. And then I had a masters in security. I also specialized in criminology, so I had that degree as well. That's the extent of my educational background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, can you tell the Chamber, please, how long have you been involved with the police, and then after that, when you became a member of the special police.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I have been working for the police since 1991. As soon as I completed the specialist training, I became a member of the special police branch. I went through all the different levels on the special police from the police -- policemen training on the job, through to the regular police work onto the head of the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In what year did you become a member of the special police, and where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: In 1991, I became a member of the special police branch of the Kutina police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: How long were you a member of the special police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I remained a special policeman until 2004, when I was transferred to the post of the chief of the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that's what -- where you currently are, as chief of police administration in Koprivnica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As part of your training as a special policeman, did you receive instructions regarding the rules and laws of warfare?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Right at the first course I attended, the first training I attended, we received instructions on how we were supposed to proceed in accordance with the legal provisions and Geneva Conventions. In addition that, prior to being dispatched on missions, we were given verbal instructions about the respect for international humanitarian law and the related Croatian legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask Madam Usher with the court's permission to give Mr. Vurnek a binder of materials, so it might be easier for him to follow, Your Honour, if that is permissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you're going to get a binder of materials some of which we might be referring to, including your witness statement, which is D1895. If we could look at your witness statement, please, and pull up page 2 of D1895. In paragraph 2 it's noted that: "Several days before Operation Storm most of the unit and I arrived on orders on Mount Velebit, where we started making preparations for the operation." Mr. Vurnek, just so you know, I will be alternating between your statement and exhibits, so if we could please go to P1241, the second page, please. Mr. Vurnek, P1241 is the war path history of the special police unit of Sisak and Moslavina. Had you had a chance to look at this document before coming to testify?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I had, yes. I had seen this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Since I've seen it only recently, I am familiar with it. I have to say that the first part relates to the Sisak group, because the special police unit of the Sisak-Moslavina area was divided into two groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that at least as far as paragraph 1 is concerned that the -- by order dated July 30, 1995, the special police from Sisak, including your Kutina unit, was ordered to move out to Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the fourth paragraph it's noted: "Together with the Kutina group at the second auxiliary axis, the unit had the task to carry out a rapid and surprising advance along the axis: Veliki Golic, Liscana Draga, Siolovici, Pilar, all the way to the eastern hills above the Gospic-Gracac road."

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please turn to 65 ter 01356. Before we get into this document, Mr. Vurnek, I'd like to ask you, and I'm again referring to paragraph 2 of your statement, were you present in Stari Grad for the commander meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: At the commanders' meeting held in Stari Grad, there was my immediate commander, and I stayed back with my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And where was that located? Where was your unit located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It's the general area of Velike Vrsine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that in the Velebit mountains?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 2 it's noted that when your commander returned from this meeting, he talked about what your tasks and obligations were. Can you describe that meeting that you had when your commander came back from Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I can. On his return from the meeting in Stari Grad, the commander gathered the whole unit and acquainted the unit leaders and all police officers with the impending tasks. Once he let us know what our tasks would be and the security measures taken, he told us that we had the obligation to abide by the provisions of the international laws of war and the legislation, the Croatian legislation in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, if we can look at the document on the screen now, which is 65 ter 01356, this is a portion of the Kutina unit's war path report; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You're familiar with this document as well, are you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The first part of the document states that you received an order on the 4th of August to begin the liberation action Oluja, and it's described upon which axes - there were three - that your unit was to engage. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you had 136 total members in your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can go -- and I'm referring to paragraph 4 of your statement, and then I'm also -- we don't need to put the statement on the screen. But paragraph 4 of your statement and in conjunction with 65 ter 01356 which is on the screen, the first day of Operation Storm, August 4th, you had your primary task was on the first axis Velike Vrsine, Crni Vhr, of your unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to read part of 65 ter 01356 and then I'm going to ask you specifically about some information relating to that. The document reads: "The first group, 35 staff members strong, under the command of specialised training instructions Trpimir Bakaric and Zlatko Felja deploys the position under Crni Vhr and guides and corrects our battery's artillery fire from there. And before I continue, the first thing I'd like to ask you, Mr. Vurnek, is it stated "deploys the position under Crni Vrh." Can you give the Trial Chamber an idea of what kind of terrain we're talking about here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Crni Vrh is the dominant feature on Mount Velebit overlooking the area and from which the enemy force was able to control the entire area and prevent the Croatian police from gaining access to the area under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of altitude are we talking about here, in this area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I'm not positive about it, I think that it's something in excess of a thousand metres; though I repeat, I'm not sure. However, the point is that there were very well fortified military features up there, complete with weapons which enabled them to control all the approach areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The second part of that sentence reads: "... guides and corrects our battery's artillery fire from there." Can you please describe what that means from your perspective. What is guiding and correcting the battery's artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The special police units attached to police administration, there were -- administrations, there were operative reconnaissance groups which were tasked with pin-pointing the exact position of the enemy force. As a rule, they moved ahead of the rest of the forces, pin-pointed the enemy positions, and guided precision artillery fire against the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the targets that they were guiding the artillery to, what kind of targets were those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: They were fortified bunkers, but specifically the ones we're referring to at Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: From where were the artillery fire coming? That means your forces artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: They were mortar batteries. I'm not sure about the position where they were embedded. But for the most part they were short-range rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'll continue with 65 ter 0356, mentions your name, Mr. Vurnek, as assistant commander was also in the group despite he suffered a leg injury, due to which his leg was partially immobilized. After several salvos, we started ascending towards the enemy's entrenched and fortified positions. Approximately 100 metres before the enemy's positions, we came across a strong minefield, which we started de-mining. At that very moment, a strong rifle fire was opened at our staff, so we moved [sic] down the slope towards the forest, where we find even more pressure-activates anti-personnel mines, so-called 'kuruzi,' on our way. We remove them all, still ascending towards the top." Now describe for us, Mr. Vurnek, if you can, how had you to deal with these minefields, if you could just describe to the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Could you repeat the first part of the question. There may have been a confusion in terms of interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. After I read that particular section and specifically referring to de-mining the minefields, can you describe what that process was under fire?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Crni Vrh that we referred to was a fortified facility surrounded by several minefields. One of the tasks of the reconnaissance operative group which went ahead was to de-mine a passage through the minefields. Later on in the report, we stated the exact positions of the minefields, and that information was passed on to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the information you got at Stari Grad on enemy positions, what unit of the special police provided you with that information?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The information on the enemy forces were given to us at the meeting with the unit commander, once he had returned from Stari Grad. It is then that he forwarded that information to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what from -- from part of the special police this intelligence information was gathered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: In the special police sector within the Ministry of Interior, there was an internal control department tasked with collecting data about the enemy and its positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We've heard a great deal of testimony about the internal control unit and seen documents as well. I'm not going to get into that specifically with you, Mr. Vurnek. But as a chief of police of Koprivnica and as a member of the special police until 2004, can you tell the Chamber whether or not, in your experience, the internal control unit was ever involved in the imposition or investigation of discipline within the special police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. In the Ministry of Interior, attached to the minister's cabinet, there was the internal control department which had to do with any disciplinary proceedings and measures to be taken against police members. I think the internal control department within the special police was exclusively tasked with information gathering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now going back to the document on the screen, Mr. Vurnek, if we could go to the next page in Croatian, please. And the next page in English. Continuing with this document, Mr. Vurnek, and there's further discussion about people being wounded as a result of -- of mines. Eventually your unit occupied Crni Vrh and captured some weaponry. As well, later in the paragraph, and I'll read, it says in the middle of the very long paragraph: "We come across the communication towards the village of Egeljac, get over it and ten metres further, we proceed going parallel with it towards the village, through high grass and vegetation. Just nearby the houses, from a distance of 10 or 15 metres, a strong submachine fire was opened at our group ..." Now, when you describe this communication -- or when it's described the communications towards the village of Egeljac, what does the report mean by that? Is that a communication line? Is that a road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As it road between Gracac and Obrovac, via Mount Velebit. Partially it's a tarmac road, and partially it's a dirt road. It traverses Mali Alan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Further, one of your members of your unit, Mr. Bakaric is killed in action, and as you're waiting for other groups to link up, your unit ended up capturing two T-55 tanks and an armoured personnel carrier. Could you describe what happened involving that capture and what lead to that capture.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: First, I have so say the following the village of Egeljac, actually comprises of two houses, it's a very small place. The advance party of the tank group as well as the forces which had withdrawn from Crni Vhr had set up an ambush in the immediate vicinity of those two houses. Upon our arrival, in their vicinity, they opened heavy fire on the entire column. On that occasion the group commander, Trpimir Bakaric was killed. We returned fire. After the wounded staff member was being administered help because he was still alive at the time, some reserve forces came in, as well as parts of the Vukovar-Srijem unit. We continued our movement together against the group which had set up the ambush. We broke them up and seized the two tanks. So it wasn't only the Kutina group that did that but also some of our Vinkovac [phoen] colleagues helped in the capturing of the two tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And during this entire time you participated while you were wounded in action.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I had a fractured leg, I was not wounded. I had a plaster cast on. It was not a result of a wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you end up in this report -- the unit ends up at the Gracac-Gospic communication. Can you describe what that is, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That road spans across the territory between Gracac and Gospic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The last sentence of this paragraph states: "Here we place a BBP around 2100 hours, in the way that the SJP Vinkovci part towards Gospic and we towards Gracac." Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what a BPP is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Blockade command -- sorry, blockade combat point of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe what that is to the Chamber, your understanding of what a BBP is. What does it entail?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The tasks of those manning a BPP is simply to protect and keep the line that had been reached. A barrier check-point is something that no one should go beyond, save for a unit which is supposed to advance further or is returning, as opposed to a checkpoint of the police which is set up exclusively by jointly the civilian and military police in order to exercise control of those going through that point. In other words, one is not supposed to go through a combat barrier point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We've seen in other reports this described as a BPP. Is the BBP and the BPP essentially the same thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't know what the background of this sentence is. Unfortunately, I cannot answer that question. I would have to see the entire text to see what it refers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber whether the special police held any types of check-points jointly with any other forces. Meaning military police or civil police.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Not in Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, we've heard testimony from various internationals that people described as special police at check-points were wearing grey or silver or blue uniforms. Can you tell the Chamber during the course of Operation Storm and afterwards, what types of uniforms the special police would be wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: To repeat, the special police did not man check-points. It had no tasks there. During Operation Storm, the special police wore exclusively the green special police uniform with all the insignia that is usually found on those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, during and after Operation Storm was there ever an occasion that you can recall that a special police unit would wear camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, the end of the first day of Operation Storm, your unit was where? If you could tell the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: At the end of the first day, part of the unit had deployed along the road between Gracac and Gospic setting up two combat barrier points. Another part, including myself, remained where the captured tanks were on orders of the special police sector commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So essentially at the end of the first day, the forces spend the evening essentially outside?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Out in the open. We slept in the forest or in the meadows nearby, in difficult conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Through this point, Mr. Vurnek, had your unit encountered any civilians?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for the Chamber the nature of this area. Was it heavily populated, lightly populated, unpopulated?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: During the first day of the operation, we covered mainly forested area next to Mount Velebit. There was the odd house here and there along the way. In any case, there were no densely populated locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The second day in paragraph 5 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I please tender 65 ter 1356.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1896. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, in paragraph 5 of your statement you talk about the second day of the operation and you continued towards Gracac, entering at about 1400 hours, and at least on the way to Gracac there were no combat operations. Could you please describe for the Chamber what you saw as you got into Gracac from your positions the evening before? What your observations were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We entered Gracac around 2.00 p.m. Once we were there, I was able to see one house that had been set alight. I don't know when that started, but by that time, it had burnt -- well, most of it was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were your units the first units to enter Gracac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No. Gracac had already been liberated, and there was no one there. No enemy forces and no civilians that could I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon entering Gracac, was there anything that was discovered in terms of weapons or storage facilities that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of the burning house, there was a factory, I believe, I don't know what it produced. But they had relatively large hangars. We were trying to find some fire extinguishers, and it was for that reason that we entered the factory. Inside, we found a large amount of weapons, pieces of weapons, and a full ammunition depot. We didn't check the crates themselves, but I know that they must have contained explosives and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As you entered Gracac town itself, can you describe what you saw, in terms of damage.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The burning house was the only damage I could see. Along the road, I noticed a number of craters, in particular close to an intersection. But one could not ascertain whether these were new or older crates [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: During your time -- the rest of that day, which was the second day of Operation Storm, that night of August 5th and the entire next day of August 6th was spend in Gracac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes, the unit was resting.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 19, line 7, it should be craters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: During your entire time in Gracac, did you observe at any time any members of the special police either burning buildings or looting buildings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you housed in -- in Gracac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: In the town centre, in the court-house, I believe, or -- it was either that or some kind of public facility. That was on one day. On the other day, we were in the school. It was also a public facilitate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived Gracac, was -- did you have a chance to basically change into different kinds of footgear and gear that was different from what you had when you were up in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes. We had very good logistics. Shortly after we had liberated the roads we have referred to, our forces brought in fresh clothes, footwear, we were able to rest, shower, and change, in order to pursue our activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on the 7th of August, in paragraph 7, which is the fourth day of Operation Storm, you were ordered to Bruvno. Can you explain what the reasoning was behind being ordered to Bruvno.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: My unit was organised as a reserve force in the course of Mazin being liberated. Immediately next to Bruvno, on a nearby meadow, we waited for the units which were liberating Mazin to complete their operation. After it was liberated, we continued our advance in front of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you advised or did you expect any kind of counter-attack from Donji Lapac area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: There was an expectation of a strong counter-attack from Donji Lapac. However, it never materialised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, on your way from Gracac to Bruvno to Mazin, can you describe to the Trial Chamber how you got there? Was it walking, was it in trucks? Can you describe how you got there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: From Gracac to the position just above Mazin towards Dobroselo, we went in vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of vehicles were these?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The vehicles we had in the unit. That is to say, military trucks and a civilian van, as well as several passenger vehicles with police plates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, as you were proceeding to Bruvno and Mazin, can you describe to the Trial Chamber whether any members of the special police were involved in any burning of buildings or looting of properties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Nothing was on fire. There was no burning of any buildings. There was a meadow just before entering Mazin. I see -- I saw a haystack that was on fire, but there was no burning of houses or looting. Special forces were not involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go back to D18 -- we'll stay where we are right now. If we could please pull up 65 ter 00110. It takes a while because it's a map. Should be on the last page in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you can see here 65 ter 00110. On the top right, the thick line is the border between Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. The arrow at the right points toward Kulen Vakuf, which is in Bosnia. The arrow beneath that arrow which is on the top right is -- just to the left of arrow is Boricevac, if you can see that. Right now it's basically in the middle of the page on the screen. At -- near the bottom of that arrow where Boricevac is, it says Lapac, but that is Gornji Lapac. And if you make a 45-degree angle, the arrow on the left there, that's Donji Lapac. Do you see those points, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I can see Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the road from --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: And Gornji Lapac as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The arrow, not the far left arrow but the arrow which is essentially --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down on that a little bit, please. There we go, we can stop right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The arrow -- there are two arrows in the left bottom part of the screen. The arrow on the right is on Mazin. Do you see that, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now your unit was one of the units that went on this area from Mazin to Gornji Lapac; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And between Mazin and Gornji Lapac, and unfortunately we can't see that on the map, is a place called -- oh, yes, we can. We can see Dobroselo which is along the road from Donji Lapac going from left to right at a 45-degree angle. Dobroselo, there's a little circle there near Dobroselo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll up a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's right in the middle of where the screen is. Do you see that, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Trial Chamber from Mazin to Gornji Lapac what your observations were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: What is missing here is the movement of my unit along a road. As we descended down the winding road between Mazin and Dobroselo, on the right-hand side of the road, we were able to see a mixed column of civilians and enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, Mr. Vurnek, you'll be able to draw on a map - doesn't have to be an exact science here - but essentially draw on the screen the direction of your unit toward Dobroselo. If could you do that, please. Before doing that, Your Honour, I would like to tender the map as it is as an exhibit, and then I will tender the drawing as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the map marked by whom, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This particular map was part of D1896, part of the war path report, Your Honour. And I just want to make it a separate exhibit, since we have referred to it specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the map marked, although not by the witness, would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D1897. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1897 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vurnek, if you could on the screen draw generally how your unit proceeded toward Dobroselo from Mazin.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I have to emphasise the fact that I will be doing from memory and I'm not sure that that's really the case. So we went along the road and onwards towards Dobroselo. As we descended from this position, along the road we saw a departing column.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a technical problem because the marking now appears from what I see on the text in e-court which ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, no one is going to grade you on your drawing, so don't worry, we'll see if we can get these technical things settled, and then you can ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone is working hard to get it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Need a hard copy. All right. Put it on the ELMO, and then we'll scan it later. That's fine. You can use mine, if that is all right, Your Honour, we can use --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that. It's unfortunate that, technically, it's -- I do not understand why -- what always works well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's why I became a lawyer, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I still do not know whether that was the right choice for you or for me, Mr. Kuzmanovic. A disadvantage being that it is far more difficult to make any corrections to -- But let have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher, for helping.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As we said, Mr. Vurnek, you don't need to be exact, but please draw, if you can, the best way on this particular map your unit took from Mazin to Dobroselo. You are going to have draw directly on the document itself on the apparatus there. For some reason the screen isn't working properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a problem with the ELMO as well. I see on whatever button I push -- yes. Now, apparently ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There we go. If we could turn it 90 degrees to the right. There we go. Thank you. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you've marked in red on this particular document as best approximation as you can along that winding road from Mazin overlooking Dobroselo. Now, the column of refugees that they saw, in which direction were they travelling? Were they travelling essentially from left to right? If you look at the map, it would be from north-west to south-east?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As we're looking at the map, they were to our right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that road goes where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I think it goes to Srb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, after you reached Dobroselo, can you describe for the Trial Chamber where you went -- strike that. After coming close to Dobroselo, did you have the opportunity to observe two communications operatives in a jeep?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Before we descended toward Dobroselo, and since I was among the ones who were at the head of the column, I didn't see how many individuals were in the all-terrain vehicle, but I did see the vehicle pass us and continue toward Dobroselo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see whether that vehicle -- where the vehicle went after reaching Dobroselo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Our communications officers were in the vehicle. I don't know why they had to overtake our column, but as they reached Dobroselo, they turned right in the direction of the column that was just about to leave Dobroselo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe to the Chamber what you saw in that column, what kind of vehicles, what kind of people were in that column?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It was a mixed column of various military vehicles and civilians who, for the most part, drove tractors and cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I neglected to move the map into evidence that Mr. Vurnek drew. I would like do move that, please, tender that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map marked by the witness, Mr. Registrar, would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1898.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Although, Mr. President, usually it's the Defence who uses blue, so for once I think it is the opposite colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour, we -- since we didn't have that colour on the screen available to us on the screen, I think Madam Usher just gave him what was available on the desk. So no blame to go around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps better to find the right colour first. But what was marked red was marked at the request of the Markac Defence. Just for my understanding, is it the understanding of the parties that the winding road down, is that the one initially marked M3 and then further on 4M3? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the road. Now could the witness -- apart from that, there is no problem in admitting it into evidence. The witness said he saw the column to his right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We can be more specific, Your Honour, if you would like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we -- is that a road which is called 8A7? Is that a road or ... Could we ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you heard His Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And they were moving in a south-easterly direction, then, from what I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar -- Well, no, I think the map received a number already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think we marked it, but Mr. Registrar's mike wasn't working at the time, so I don't know if it was heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what we have on the record at this moment. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was D1898, Your Honour, on line 15, page 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, D1898 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, using the map that's on the screen which is D1897, your units then when to Gornji Lapac, which is essentially the arrow -- right near the arrow which is in the middle, upper middle left of the map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did your unit ever enter Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No, the unit I was in command of was not in Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now when you were in Donji Lapac can you please tell the Trial Chamber what your observations were. I'm sorry, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Wasn't in Donji Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you entered Gornji Lapac, can you please tell the Chamber what your observations were.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We only marginally entered Donji Lapac [as interpreted] because as we arrived from the direction of Dobroselo we turned for Kulen Vakuf. At the junction from where the road leads to Donji Lapac, I saw a destroyed truck belonging to the enemy and a great amount of ammunition and explosives strewn around the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, as you progressed from Gornji Lapac to Kulen Vakuf, where did you end up spending the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We reached Stari Grad at Kulen Vakuf on that same day. We set up combat barrier points and spent the night in the forest there, in the vicinity of these barrier points.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In and around Kulen Vakuf, was there any enemy fire that you encountered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We didn't go into town itself. As we were on our way to Kulen Vakuf, the old town, we didn't come across any armies or civilians, save for one horse-drawn cart that had been run over by a tank because you could see the marks of Caterpillar tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: From the time that you entered Gracac through the time that you left to return to your home unit, had you called in any artillery fire or use artillery, your particular unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No. We didn't come across any resistance. There was no fighting, and, therefore, there was no call for any support.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraph 8 you describe that on the 8th or 9th of August you handed your positions and returned to base in Kutina. To whom did you hand your positions? Do you remember which unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't remember which unit that was. But I think it was a Home Guard Regiment or something like that. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you under any enemy tank fire at any point in time between Gornji Lapac and Kulen Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As we were erecting combat barrier points around the perimeter of Kulen Vakuf, we came under heavy tank and mortar enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was before you spent the evening in and the area of -- around the area of Kulen Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Right after we took up positions. And throughout the following day there was artillery fire. So the attack did not cease.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, your unit then went back to Kutina after, on the 8th or 9th of August. Can you please describe what route your unit took to return to Kutina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We went back via Plitvice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you have returned through Gracac, or would have you returned through Udbina?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Through Udbina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vurnek, your unit, at some point after Operation Storm, was involved in mop-up operations; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe where you were involved in mop-up operations, first of all; and then after you tell us that, please tell us what you did in mop-up operations.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I, myself, was engaged in mop-up operations of the area. Our primary task was to uncover the remaining groups of enemy soldiers, to find explosives depots, and to pin-point minefields in the area. Those were our basic tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you engaged in mop-up operations in and around the area of Gracac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did those mop-up operations occur sometime toward the end of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was your unit involved in the mop-up operation of either Petrova Gora or Plitvice?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Petrova Gora, yes; and I don't remember about Plitvice, though I presume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, can you -- the final question I wanted to ask you was about General Markac. Could you please -- before I ask you that question, the area of Petrova Gora was in sector -- what was called Sector North, correct, at one time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the Plitvice operation which you said that you weren't necessarily sure if you personally participated in, was that also on the edge of the northernmost zone of the Split-Gospic Military District -- or the Gospic Military District, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I am certain that I did not participate in the Plitvice operation since I was occupied elsewhere. But I assume that my unit engaged in the searches of the Plitvice areas. I believe that it is right on the edge of the Gospic area, though I'm not positive about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vurnek. The last question or set of questions I wanted to ask you before we take a break involves General Markac, your experience with him. And I'd like you, please, to be -- to describe to the Chamber what kind of person General Markac was and is, in terms of character and professionalism and your dealings with him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: General Markac, assistant minister during the war, well, my personal opinion, is that he is a top-notch strategist, operative, and very good at tactics. He is good with people. He is a top professional. I can tell that you before I got to know General Markac and before he retired, I had never, within the system of the Ministry of Interior, met a better professional than him. Counsel, I am truly proud and happy to have been able to be special policeman under General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vurnek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. In view of the time, first of all, have the other Defence teams any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we won't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. De Landri, I think it would be better to first have a break and that you cross-examine the witness after the break. Mr. Kuzmanovic, the Chamber was informed that there are no other witness available for today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's true, Your Honour. Unfortunately, given what happened last week, we had to do some juggling and the next witness who is supposed to testimony MM-025 is arriving today and that witness will be ready to testify tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. De Landri, could you give the Chamber any impression as to how much time you would need in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I expect to be one session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One full session. Then we will take a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, you will now be cross-examined by Ms. De Landri. Ms. De Landri is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, I would like to ask you some questions about the statement that you gave, and in particular, can you tell the Chamber who was present when you gave your statement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Counsel, Tomislav Kuzmanovic and Vlado Rendulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Was anyone else present?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: At the time the statement was being taken, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to, if Mr. Registrar could pull up the D1895, excuse me, on the screen. And if the witness, if would you direct your attention to the cover sheet of the Croatian version. In addition to your name and the other two names you've just mentioned, I believe there's a fourth name there. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who that individual is? Can you read that name and tell us who that individual is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Djurica Franjo. He came to the administration with the gentlemen but was not present when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And do you know who that individual is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I saw him twice. I have a feeling that I would occasionally see him earlier on, but I hadn't met him officially.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Do you recall when the first time you met him was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The first time I met him was several months before the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And could you give the Chamber an approximate date of when you met him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell the Chamber the circumstances when you met him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I seek the relevance of these questions relating to Mr. Djurica. I mean, what is the relevance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Djurica is -- Franjo is reported to be present, and the witness says he was not present. And the role of Djurica Franjo during the events might have some relevance for his presence or non-presence. Therefore, Ms. De Landri, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I believe there's a question pending.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us the circumstances under which you met the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: When I was asked for the first time to appear as a Defence witness on behalf of Mr. Markac, he visited me and explained what such a testimony should look like.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And what did he tell you at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: To be honest, I can't recall. I seem to recall the presence of another female and Mr. Soljic was there as well. I mostly discussed matters with Mr. Soljic, since I had not known Mr. Djurica Franjo from before.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: What did you understand his position to be? Mr. Franjo's position, that is.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what his role is. I suppose he's a member of the team for the Defence of General Markac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Did you ask him at that time what his position was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And did there come a time when you saw him again?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I saw him later, when I was giving the statement. But I don't remember him being present at the moment when I was giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I guess I'm -- I'm not quite clear on what your answer to the question is. You -- you said you saw him later, but you didn't remember. So do you not recall him being present when the statement was given?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I'm not 100 percent certain. He was there in the period when I was giving the statement, but I don't remember him -- him being there at the moment of giving my statement as such. I simply recall Mr. Kuzmanovic and another counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And who asked you questions during the time you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And did anyone else ask you questions during the time you gave your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. So it's possible that someone else did ask you questions.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Not in the formal process of giving the statement. It is possible that other people put questions to me in an informal setting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- when you say that other people may have put questions to you in an informal setting, would you tell the Trial Chamber about those kinds of settings.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Well, we discussed my recollection of taking part in Operation Storm. But it was an informal discussion and simply the things that I could remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we," you're talking about yourself and who?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Countless times I discussed that. Regarding this specific discussion, the persons stated on the statement were there, and I think one or two other work-mates of mine from the police administration were present during the informal discussions.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: So that would include Mr. Franjo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And how many times did you discuss your participation in Operation Storm with Mr. Franjo?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Personally, I never discussed it with him. He was present, as I say, but I don't remember him putting any questions to me, and I don't remember discussing that with him. All communication basically took place between me and the counsel, as well as Mr. Soljic during the first meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Chamber if you've seen Mr. Franjo since you gave your statement in this case?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Are you sure that you have not seen him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't remember having seen him anywhere. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to direct your attention to --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Apologies, apologies. I did see him once, in Zagreb, after giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And can you describe the circumstances of when and where you saw him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: We were in a restaurant having lunch in Petrinjska Street. I don't remember the name of the restaurant anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And did you talk?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And that was the only time you've seen him since giving the statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Have you spoken with him on the phone since giving the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Have you exchanged any correspondence with him since then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to direct your attention to the substance of your statement. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, if you would allow, I would like to put a few further questions in relation to the matter you have apparently --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that you were in a restaurant having lunch in Petrinjska Street, did have you lunch with Mr. Djurica Franjo, or did you have lunch with others and that you -- was he was seated at another table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he was seated at the same table, but there were around 20 people there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And at what occasion was this lunch organised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, Your Honour, I don't know what it was in relation to. In any case I was invited to that lunch, and I went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By whom were you invited?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By Counsel Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any other former colleagues of yours present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were several of my colleagues present during the lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did that lunch take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think about two months ago, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there any other persons present of whom you learned or perhaps already knew at the time that they would testify before this Tribunal called by the Markac Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later on, I learned that Mr. Pavlovic was to be, or had already been a witness in these proceedings. He was one of the people in attendance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other persons of who you know that they are witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know of anyone else being a witness in these proceedings who attended that lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you do not remember who were there, or because you do not know that -- whether or not they are witnesses in this -- called by the Markac Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think both. I don't know who all of the witnesses are. It is quite customary down there to go and have lunch daily almost, to associate, socialise ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How often did you attend lunch apart from this occasion with the Markac Defence team or members of the Markac Defence team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once in Zagreb; and twice in Koprivnica, when they came to see me in the police administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us about the informal meetings, or whatever you want to call them, before the statement was taken. Was that on the same day the statement was taken, or was that the day before, or the days before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If you mean the occasion on which the statement was taken, an informal meeting or perhaps not even a meeting, but having lunch together is something that took place after the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you earlier said -- I'm now not talking specifically about lunch meetings, but you earlier said -- I have difficulties in manipulating my ... You said that you were -- spoke about the events in meetings prior to the official statement being taken. You said when Mr. Djurica Franjo was present as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. The first time, when Mr. Soljic and Mr. Djurica Franjo visited me, there was another female person, and they came to ask me whether I wished to appear as witness before this Tribunal. I consented to that, under certain conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Those conditions being?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first condition was that I tell the truth the way I saw it. That is to say, that I shouldn't be prompted or anything should be suggested to me to influence my memory. The other condition was to have a full audio and video recording and that I be provided with a copy of that recording of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're talking about the recording of your testimony, not of the interviews held.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were my conditions. And Mr. Soljic answered to that, that concerning my first condition, no one was ever to suggest anything to me. As for the second part, he told me that I was to receive a written copy; in other words, that they couldn't meet my second condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asking to have your interview being recorded. That correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was denied.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't reject that, but they said that they would draft a statement and that I would receive a copy in written form. I agreed to that, and I was happy with that solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now that was the first time that they came to see you to ask whether you wanted to testify. How long did that meeting take and when took this meeting place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see that as a -- as a formal meeting. It was a simple discussion during which I was asked whether I wished to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just asked when it took place and how long it took.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That conversation took place a few months before the formal giving of the statement. It lasted for -- well, anywhere between quarter of an hour and half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the lady who was present was whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honour, I don't know her name and what her role was. I suppose, although I don't know, that she's also a member of the team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the next time that you met with members of the team before, as you said, the formal interview took place, when was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the day when I gave my statement, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us in more detail who were present during that meeting before the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Kuzmanovic came, as well as Mr. Rendulic and Mr. Franjo came to the police administration. As for the giving of the statement itself, I don't think he was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you earlier said that former colleagues of yours were present as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After I gave the statement, yes. They were not former colleagues; they are my current colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have problems with my LiveNote, and I have to rely on it at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have problems with my e-court, which disables me to literally quote, but let's try to make the best out of it. You were interviewed in the -- on the premises of the police administration; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time did the gathering take where you informally discussed matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there an explanation as to why Mr. Djurica Franjo then left when the statement was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know him. I don't even notice him around. I did not exchange more than a couple of sentences in my life with him. He was simply around there, but I paid no heed. It wasn't important to me whether he was there or somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kuzmanovic was present; Mr. Rendulic was present; you were present. And then who that other person was when you were about to give an interview didn't -- you didn't care about that? You're not interested. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kuzmanovic is Mr. Markac's counsel, and, as such, I believe, the most important person in that setting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not my question, as a matter of fact, who was the most important, but whether you did care or not. I apologise for not being that much concentrated, but my system is now working again. Yes, you said you discussed your recollection. Could you give us a bit more details about discussing your recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have in mind the informal part of the meeting? I am unclear about the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have the informal part of the meeting in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour, I did not understand the question. The informal part was over lunch where we discussed not the matters I mentioned in the statement or anything in particular concerning that, but we discussed matters in general: Operation Storm and the current activities of the police administration and life in general. However, as I said, it was over lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that a lunch where your colleagues were present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You earlier said that it was after your interview. And now you -- your answer suggests that it was before the interview.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The informal socialising took place after the interview and once the statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, I earlier asked you: "And could you tell us in more detail who were present during that meeting before the statement was taken?" And then you said: "Counsel Kuzmanovic came as well as Mr. Rendulic and Mr. Franjo came to the police administration." You didn't say that you did not meet them before the statement was taken; you just answered my question by telling who were present. Could you -- do you remember at what time you met on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. It could have been 10.00, 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, during the last lunch you described that was the occasion where you saw Mr. Djurica Franjo again, you were 20. Could you, to the best of your recollection, tell us who were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact number of persons present there. I remember my colleague Vrsaljko being there. Attorney Rendulic, Kuzmanovic, I, Djurica, Pavlovic. Two more persons with Vrsaljko whom I didn't know. These are the individuals I can think of. Excuse me, Soljic was there too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Pejkovic there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He may have been among the individuals unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know Mr. Pejkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, no, I don't know who he is. Perhaps if I saw his photograph, I might recognise him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vitez, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. De Landri.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mr. Vurnek, in your statement you said that the day before Operation Storm your commander spoke to you and members of your unit about respecting the international law of war. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And did you, at all times, abide by those laws and obligations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And did you observe members of your unit abiding by those obligations and rules?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And what about other members of special police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The ones I know of, they all did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: What about the ones that you personally observed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: They all absolutely adhered to the international law of war. All those I was able to observe.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could I have P2373, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And, Mr. Vurnek, I'd ask you to look at the first page of this document and ask you if you've ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I think I did. I have seen it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And just direct your attention to the second page in -- second page in the English and it's also the second page in the B/C/S.
