I'm just going to ask you a few questions about this document. In particular, the document refers to, and I quote: "The situation with discipline in 1995 is slowly deteriorating ... it is slowly getting worse towards the end of the year. This worsening is the result of an unsettled situation at the unit command. "One of the problems that influences discipline in the unit are members who have been in the unit for a long time (a part of the members from 1991, both active and reserve). A part of those members, including several VSG/special groups leaders, very rarely or never take part in training, and spend most of their working hours in the bar at the base." When did you join the unit, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I joined the special police branch in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And did you observe any of the problems discussed in this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: If you will allow me to, I have to provide a longer explanation to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: The special unit of the Sisak-Moslavina police administration consisted of two elements: One belonged to Sisak and the other to Kutina. This particular report relates to the situation in the special unit of the Sisak-Moslavina police administration, its Sisak element. In other words, that's not the unit I was a member of, and we didn't have such details as are mentioned here. The only thing we shared in common was the commander. The units were both deployed to different locations. I was assistant commander for the Kutina group, and this has to do with the Sisak group.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: When you say you shared the commander, would that have been the commander who issued the orders after the briefing that's referred to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask answer other question about this document, and it's on the second page of the English. I believe it's on the third page of the B/C/S. In the middle of the third page of the English, there's a reference to: "General problems of the active section are mainly related to housing and the status of the special MUP units after the end of war activities. Housing problems are particular because many members looked for accommodation in the houses in the liberated area during the military-police Operation Storm, and they have problems with clearance for them. People feel insecure regarding a positive solution of that problem because there are cases that the owners of those houses returned from Serbia. Additional concern was caused by removing these members from the housing lists" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: "... in the unit." Did you observe any such problems?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Let me repeat, the Kutina group did not have such problems. But if you will allow me to, I can give you assumption of what this may be about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. De Landri, if you are reading you go too quick, and the interpreters can not follow you. Could you please, so in order to make absolutely sure that we have -- could you please repeat the last part of your quotation and then see whether we have anything -- everything complete.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Let me place my question in the context again. And I understand that you have said that this document did not relate to your specific unit, but I want to -- the information that I'm trying to -- that I'm trying to -- to probe is, did you have any -- did you observe these problems that are referred to here? And I will quote the document again. The document says: "General problems of the active section are mainly related to housing and the status of special MUP units after the end of war activities. Housing problems are particular because many members looked for accommodation in the houses in the liberated area during the military-police Operation Storm, and they have problems with clearance for them. People feel insecure regarding a positive solution of that problem because there are cases that the owners of those houses return from Serbia." And my question to you, sir, is: I understand that this document does not specifically relate to your unit but you shared the same commander with this unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And did you interact with men from this unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Occasionally. With leaders, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And I assume that you would -- that the leaders would have been -- the leaders of that unit would have been aware of the units discussed in this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I assume that they were aware of them and that they were dealing with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And did they ever discuss these problems with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions about your statement again in this case. Did you have an opportunity to review your statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And were you given the opportunity to make changes to the statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know if there is such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, you were present when the statement was made; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes. And I stand by my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. So you were -- you were able to assure that the contents of it were completely accurate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I think that the contents of it are -- are accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And did counsel show it to you after it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And were you given the opportunity to make changes to it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As I said, there was no need for it. There were certain details that I could think of subsequently. After all, it's been a long time. But whatever the case, I stand by the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. So just to be clear: You were given the opportunity to make changes to your statement and to make sure that it was complete and accurate at the time you gave the statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this morning, Mr. Kuzmanovic asked you some questions about August 5th and Gracac. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And your testimony - and I'm not going to quote it - but included reference to seeing one structure burning and that you and, I believe, some other members of the special police went into a factory to look for fire extinguishers, and you found some ammunition or some other weapons. Is that correct? Am I, in substance, summarizing your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Can you take a look at your statement now. Can we have that on the screen. I believe it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Just one moment. That's D1895.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And, in particular, I would like to direct your attention to paragraph 5 of the statement. Have you had an opportunity to look at that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Is there a reference in the statement to the events that you testified about this morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: About finding the ammunition in the building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I didn't think it particularly necessary to mention that in the statement, since we found ammunition and explosives almost everywhere we went.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Now you do say here in paragraph 5 also that: "I did not see a single member of the special police destroying or stealing anyone's property." And is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Vurnek, the Trial Chamber in this case has heard evidence from a number of witnesses that there were members of the special police burning houses and looting in Gracac around the time that you were present there. And how do you respond to their observations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like some citation to the record identifying special police members burning and looting in Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Specific references.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly. P516; it's paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. P516, 41, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And there's also P322. And P321. And there are several transcript pages also; page 5424, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes. It's that one with transcript page reference, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 516, 41, does not reflect what you put to the witness, Ms. De Landri. At least I have difficulties in --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will check my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. Meanwhile, I'll check the other sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Paragraph 41, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I will turn to 321, which -- 321, and we'll have a look P321.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Right, P321.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. If you would just first allow me to -- to have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, there is P322 as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we have a reference because many of these are about 30 to 40 paragraphs long, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, 322 is just a newspaper article. It is only about three pages long, but right on the front page the first page. And the second page, the middle of the second page in the English translation. I think it was originally in Dutch. And I can give you some paragraphs in 321. Paragraph 31 identifies the special police in Gracac on August 5th. And the same witness is in -- is the author of P322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You described it - and that seems to be the problem - in a rather qualificative term, so rather than in factual terms, whereas there is quite a bit of dispute on what can be seen on some of the sources. For example, 324 is the result of what the witness said, and 321, and there has been quite a bit of dispute here and there about certain matters. So if you want to put something to the witness, then I would invite you to make it as factual as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps I could call up a photograph to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But perhaps first, then -- Mr. Vurnek, when preparing or giving your statement or when preparing for today's testimony, were any photographs shown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I saw several photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember what you could see on these photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate your asking these questions, and I have no problem with them. I think we need to establish the date when the photographs were taken and compare them to when the witness was there. And I think that is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just want to know at this moment whether any photographs were shown to the witness. And that is a matter that could have followed up my questions. If have you no problems in my question, Mr. Kuzmanovic, and if you want to draw the attention to a certain matter, rather do it at a later stage, rather than to interfere --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't mean to interfere, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you did. Could you tell us what photographs you saw. What was depicted in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw two photographs depicting a vehicle, a car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was it a passenger car, was it a truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was a black-and-white photograph. I can't tell you what colour it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the vehicle driving, was it parked, was it -- or several photographs, did you -- could you briefly describe what you saw.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw two photographs of a vehicle and a policeman in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, at the time when you were there, had you seen this vehicle or vehicles which looked, in some respects, similar to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the first time I saw the photograph, and I didn't see it in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did anyone explain to you why -- what you saw, what was the meaning of what you saw in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you form any opinion about it yourself on what -- what must it have been, if you didn't form any opinion about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would need more information to make a conclusion of that sort. Otherwise, I can only suppose what it concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what do you suppose it concerns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that the vehicle had been either abandoned or without fuel and that it needed to be removed, taken off the road, so as to free it for traffic. I must underscore that this is only my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And no one suggested that this was the meaning of that photograph to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. And I wouldn't have allowed anyone to suggest anything to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that -- did you also see that same car driving away at -- or driving in at ... was the whole series shown to you? Perhaps, Ms. De Landri, you ask for -- I figure that you were heading for P324?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, actually, I was going ask for P322.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 3 -- yes. Yes, then I let you go first.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you. 322, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps we come back later at 324.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Right. I'd like to direct your attention to this document, Mr. Vurnek, and specific parts of it, particularly the date, which is August 9, 1995. And as you can see, it's a newspaper article. It's been -- originally appeared in a Belgian newspaper. It has been translated for us into English and B/C/S. And, in particular, if you could look at the second full paragraph and just take a moment to look at that. Have you had an opportunity to read that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I have. Pardon me, Prosecutor. Do you want me to answer your previous question?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the basics first. We can agree that the article is dated August 9th; correct? Is that right? You need to say yes or no for the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It says here that it's of the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And the person who wrote it refers to the previous day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. So the events that he's writing about have occurred on or before August 8th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It say the day before, so on or before, I think it is pretty self-evident that the author is referring to August 8th. And if we could establish some foundation that Mr. Vurnek was present there on August 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: No, I appreciate counsel's observations, and I am aware of the witness's testimony about when he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether it is the day before to what that refers exactly is a matter perhaps to be explored. But I take it that this witness could not help us very much in that sense. Please proceed, Ms. De Landri.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: My next question is: in the third full paragraph -- first, were you familiar with Gracac before operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I had never been to Gracac before the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Do you know if it was a residential area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I suppose it was. I suppose it was the administrative centre of that region.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. I want to direct your attention to the third paragraph in this article. And, in particular, the first sentence of the third paragraph: "Not a single house remains intact along the 50-kilometre stretch between Gospic and Gracac." My question, based on what's contained in this article and the date of the article and the time-frame, if no houses remained in the area as of August 8th or 9th, how long do you think it might have taken for those houses to be destroyed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't think I can comment this article, given that, as of the 7th onwards we were in the direction of Kulen Vakuf. I can't comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, I'm only asking you to use the article as a time-frame, and I'm asking you to also use your presence in the area and your recollection and your personal observations to go back and answer my question. If the area was a residential area and people lived there and most of the houses were destroyed, how long would it take to accomplish that, do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think we need some foundation here as to may have conducted this campaign of destruction of houses and when -- there's no foundation as to when it occurred, how it was done --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- I think at this moment, Ms. De Landri is establishing the situation as it was found during those days and is trying to explore how quickly that situation could have changed or could not have changed. That is, apparently, what Ms. De Landri is seeking to do, and she is entitled to do that. And then who caused what and at what time is, of course, is a matter which is, to some extent, dealt with in the article. Please proceed, Ms. De Landri.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: So to go back to my question. What I'm trying to ascertain is -- in your view, and even as of 1995, you had a substantial amount of experience, is that correct, in the special police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. How long do you think it could have taken to destroy those structures?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I must confess that I do not understand the question fully. I can tell you that there were several houses along the roads. As for the amount of time one would need to do that, I don't know. It's not a residential area, if you are talking about this road between Gracac and Gospic. It entails a couple of -- a few houses, and I didn't see that all of them were burnt. All of the houses were still there.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Let me return to your statement for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And that's D1895, in the event that the witness needs to refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: You, in describing where you spent the night in Gracac, you said that -- in paragraph 5 of your statement you said you spent the night in abandoned houses in Gracac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whom those houses belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: One of the buildings was the court-house, and the other was a school. These were public buildings.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: So -- just so there's no confusion. So they were not residential houses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: There were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Can we have D1571, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: You testified this morning that your unit was involved in mopping up operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: In the operation of terrain search in the area of Petrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Just a few questions about this document. If could you take a look paragraphs 3, 4, and 5. Were you given instructions on -- as -- as part of the orders that you received from your commander at the beginning of Operation Storm, were you given these types of instructions that are reflected in this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: This order does not primarily fall within the scope of activities of the special police. If we came across bodies, we were supposed to advise the police headquarters. We were not the ones carrying out these tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Could I get D603, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I'm going direct your attention to the entry that's at 2325 hours, where it states: "In the Gracac area" - and this is August 6th - "20 bodies were cleared away." And ask you specifically, is that something that you were involved in?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No. In Gracac, I didn't see any soldiers or civilians, or killed members of their army, or killed civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell me if, what's reflected here in this document, these 20 bodies being cleared away, was in accordance with what we just saw in the prior document? Was there removal in accordance with what was reflected in the prior document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just don't see -- first of all, it's speculative; and, second of all, I don't see the relevance to this particular witness for that set of questions. If we could have the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, what's the basis -- what's the foundation for the knowledge of this witness? Or are you asking him to -- to compare documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, Judge, if he could take his headphones off, just for a second, and I'll briefly explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let first check whether the witness -- Do you understand English, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Poorly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could ask the witness already to have an early break, and that we take the break a little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could just have the 6th of August section of this to be shown on the screen. I don't think it's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we're not going discuss, or not even to suggest what should be shown on the screen or not in the presence of the witness who says that he at least understands some English. Could you already follow Madam Usher so that we have an opportunity to discuss a procedural matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, the Chamber, of course, we'd very much like the taking of evidence, the hearing of evidence not to become chaotic. Let me just focus on one of your earlier questions, which was burning houses along the road, witness -- the witness statement P321. We've seen the photographs in P323. Now, if you put everything in context, then it is clear, looking at how the witness had difficulties in getting, obtaining information, et cetera, that at least it seems not to be challenged or disputed in any way that what that witness observed was on the 8th of August. It published on the 9th, but he says it was -- I think it was Tuesday, the 8th of August, after he had -- Now, if we see in P323 a house in full flames at that moment what then -- I have difficulties in understanding any other way, that it has been, well, set on fire. Let's take a very large period of time within the 24 hours prior to that, and on my own experience, I would even say the likelihood that it was less than 12 hours seems to be quite big. Now, that means that it is limited to the 7th. So, therefore, I have some difficulties in understanding how this is something the witness should have noted. Of course, we do not know from the photographs who set it -- who set those houses ablaze. It is at least unlikely that this happened on the 5th or 6th or early on the 7th. I think the witness said that he had -- he left Karlovac on the 8th, because, on the 7th, he was still trying to get permission. So I have some difficulties in reconciling the several aspects and the suggestions which clearly are in your question. And, apparently, Mr. Kuzmanovic has some problems with that as well. Now, to ask a witness what he has seen, fine. And then, of course, then the next steps are how to interpret these observations and how to explain them. Could you help me in -- in reconciling your suggestions with what we have seen in that evidence? Your suggestion clearly being, haven't you seen people burning and looting? How is that possible if you look at what the testimony is? The testimony as far as these photographs are concerned, this "Standaard" article, the testimony of the witness is clearly 8th and publication on the 9th. And -- so, therefore, how could the witness, on an earlier date, see all that?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it may not have been a reporter; it may have been another witness, a military observer. And I will find the quotation. But he was informed, and he was the military observer in Gracac. He --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I looked at 516.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And 516 doesn't give a clear answer. If you look at paragraph 41, which I, of course, verified once have you given it. But I have not checked yet 5424, page 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: The quotation that I had in mind, Your Honour, was where the witness in 516, I believe it was, but I will double-check, where he said that one of his colleagues was informed by a member of the special police that his colleague was told by a member of the special police that they should clear out of the area because -- or they should leave the area because the special police were going to "clear it out." And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you put to the witness that the testimony says that it was burning and looting. And clearing out and burning and looting is not the same. I'm not saying that clearing out may not at occasions results in. But to say if someone says we're clearing the terrain which is -- or we have several -- we have several formulations for that. Of course, that's not a guarantee that nothing wrong happens. But to say that a clearing is another way of saying burning and looting, that seems, to me, a bit -- that needs at least some explanation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it was my intention to give the witness an opportunity to explain. I think he was given an opportunity to explain, and, you know, that he -- he can be given a further opportunity to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To explain what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: You know, what he saw in the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which seems, as you suggest, to -- is contradicted by later reports. At least -- well, let's not go through all of this in too much detail. But I -- I can't hide that there is a risk of mixing up times, places, observations, by inaccurate description of what is in that evidence. That's the reason why I earlier invited you strongly to look at the factual side rather than to the qualifications of what the witnesses would have seen, and all that in the proper time-frame. I think it's time for a break. Could you give us any estimate on how much time would you further need.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Probably about 15 minutes, 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I have about 15 minutes of re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break, and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vurnek, in your statement, you recounted that when you reached Gracac there was no combat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And that was on August 5th; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That was on the 5th of August at around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And you stayed there through August 6th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. So was there no combat during the entire time you were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No, there was no combat. The unit was resting in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And you testified earlier this morning that you observed one building burning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: As we were entering Gracac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. And I'm wondering if you noticed any corpses, dead bodies in Gracac or in the Gracac area on August 5th or 6th.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: So my question now is, the document that I showed you earlier. I believe it was D603, that referred to the clearing away of 20 dead bodies in the area of Gracac, if you have any idea, based on the observations that you made at the time you were there, on the 5th or 6th of August, where those bodies could have come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to see if we could -- if we're referring to that exhibit, I believe it's on the screen, if we could get the reference to the 6th of August on the screen both in the English and in the Croatian. And I'm sorry, if we could just establish the date, in terms of the foundation of the document and from whom to whom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just by looking at it, I take it that ... Ms. De Landri, just getting ... Could you again tell us where we find it exactly in this seven-page document.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In the English, it's on the third page, just -- the second paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Second paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And in the -- let's see. In the B/C/S it's in the numbered page 06124034. And it's the first full paragraph. Yes, please proceed, after having carefully considered the time-frame. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: My question to the witness is: Based on the observations that you made in the location when you were there on the 5th and 6th of August, can you explain how there could be 20 dead bodies in the area.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Mrs. Prosecutor, can I just observe that the document refers to the area of Petrinja and not Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm referring to the sentence that says: "In the Gracac area, 20 bodies were cleared away."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the previous paragraph, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: One further question about this document. Do you know why there would be no provisions stated in the document for investigation of the cause of death of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't know. That's within the purview of the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Is that a subject that the special police would have any kind of communication with, since you were in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Well, you were -- you, as a member of the special police, and your unit were in the area in -- in a military capacity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Yeah. And you had entered the area before the civilian police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And would it be a normal procedure for you to interact with the civilian police on these types of issues?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: If there were any fatal casualties of among the enemy soldiers, the special police staff was notified of it, who, at a later date, would engage in further dealings in relation to these individuals with the uniformed police and the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: But would it be -- do you know if is a normal procedure to investigate the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes. But that's not within the purview of the special police.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we have P617, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that document to come up, could I ask one question to you, Mr. Vurnek. If you clear away the bodies, would that not have a negative impact on what you could still establish at a later stage? Bodies being removed from where they had been found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the removal of bodies is not within the competence of the special police, as I said, and I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm not happy to interfere, but there's obviously another problem with the translation. In that document, the Croat word "asanirano" as translated like "clearing away." We all know that the process of sanitation is a process, and we heard a lot of evidence upon it. And I think the proper translation of the Croat word "asanacija" that we heard many times before in this procedure has been properly translated, and not translated like "clearing away" the bodies, because it could lead to a wrong conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, of course, still the matter remains what had then happened. But let's not stay too long with this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Vurnek, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do. But I am not able to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. When you say you're not able to read it, is that because you can't read the handwriting in the Croatian version?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It has more to do with -- well, the handwriting is pretty illegible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. I have a couple of questions about it, and if for any reason you're not able to read the handwriting, I will read it to you and the interpreters will just translate from the English. And the document is dated August 26th, 1995. And it's from the Sisak-Moslavina special police unit, and the subject of the document is: Report on the inspection of terrain, villages, and hamlets. Were you able to read that in the original?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Just -- I want to read the second sentence, and that is: "The task carried out by six groups of ten active and reserve servicemen each from the Kutina SJP, and six groups of 15 each from the Sisak SJP."

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I'm not going to proceed to read the entire document, but if the witness will take a moment to read it, I just want to direct witness's and the Court's attention to it. It recounts the survey of a certain area and the certain civilians, I believe, who were encountered in the area, male and female, and it notes their birth dates. People, who I think, we can agree, Mr. Vurnek, in 1995 even were clearly elderly. Their dates of birth were 1912, 1919, 1913. Have you been able to see that in the original?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And towards the end of the document, it says that: "No enemy soldiers were observed during activity, and there were no traces of enemy presence lately." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I note after the list of the civilians who were found and their dates of birth and where they were found, there's no reference to any treatment of them. Do you see that -- or see the absence of any reference for what was done with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It's hard to tell in this specific case. I know that when we engaged in searching the general area we came across several civilians, and we handed them over to the uniformed police, in order that they may regulate their status.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: But that was -- and I believe this is in your statement also, that that was the routine procedure, correct, to turn them over to the civilian, the regular police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That was the standard procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know why, looking at this document, these people were not turned over to the civilian or the regular police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to speak about this specific case. It is possible that the uniformed police had already had them in their records, as being present in the area searched.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. But you don't have any way of knowing that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: No, it's an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown P587, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Vurnek, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I suppose I have, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Chamber what your observations were generally regarding discipline in the special police during Operation Storm and the period immediately following?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Could we first establish the foundation because this document is obviously written two and a half months out of scope of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic, you earlier said that it's usual that counsel who takes the witness, as one says, is involved in intervening. Now, if there is a translation issue, I do not make that much of a problem out of that. But this is it apparently something that I would have expected Mr. Kuzmanovic to do, not to say that it's dramatic, but ... Please proceed. Yes, now I still have to deal with the ... But, Ms. De Landri, I do not know what questions you will be put, and I do not know what period exactly is covered by the portion you'd like to pay attention to. Would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I'm not sure my question was answered, my last question was answered. I think I -- I don't think it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly. My question was if could you tell the Chamber what your observations were generally regarding discipline in the special police during and in the period immediately following Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I have to say that, in the Kutina group I was a member of, we didn't have any problems with discipline among men, save for some minor irregularities.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Okay. Directing your attention now to the exhibit that's on the screen; that's P587. And, in particular, and I recognise that that is dated November 15th of 1995. But I would like to direct your attention in particular to paragraph 2 of the document, that's numbered paragraph 2. And that paragraph states: "Unit commanders and department heads with the special police sector shall forthwith take measures to ensure civilised, professional, and lawful execution of official assignments of the special police members, thus eliminating arrogance and haughtiness in dealings with the population." And my question about this document is -- and it is signed by Assistant Minister Markac, the record should reflect. Do you know why Mr. Markac would have issued this order if it had not been necessary?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I don't know the specific reason behind the order. What I know is that, still today, as chief of the police administration, I issue an order of this short at the monthly meeting, and it is produced in writing as well. And it is not only related to the special police but to all the police branches I am in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear on your answer. You issue an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, your question was so much at an abstract level. If not necessary, what would have been the reasons to issue something which was unnecessary? There's -- it's of an abstraction where I would not, unless the witness has any specific knowledge where this order was issued, we'd like to hear; if not, let's move on. Do you have any specific knowledge about this order, Mr. Vurnek?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But I can tell you that at our regular meetings we constantly alerted our men to the need to abide by the rules of discipline. At least that applied to the unit I was a member of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was an answer to my question. Could you please move on, Ms. De Landri.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to, I believe it is, paragraph 8 of your statement. And you will recall that you had -- or, I'm sorry, it's paragraph 9. In paragraph 9 you stated: "During the entire operation my unit neither requested nor required any artillery support." You recall that? And you were asked in your direct examination about a document. It's -- and I think we will need this document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: It's D1896.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention to the portion in the document where your name appears, Mr. Vurnek. That's both in the English and in the B/C/S. There's a reference to artillery fire. And my question is, I'm just trying to clarify, your statement says that you did not have any -- you never called on, you had no need for artillery fire, and it's unclear to me based on what is written in this document, D1896, where it says - you'll have to forgive my pronunciation - the first group 35 staff members strong, and then it mentioned several individuals, deploys the position under Crni Vrh and guides and corrects our battery's artillery fire from there. So is that -- did you in fact call for the artillery? I'm just not clear as to how that is -- how that can be harmonised with what's in paragraph 9 of your statement. Can you explain that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: This happened before the start of the operation. Artillery fire support was sought, in order to neutralize the enemy forces at Crni Vrh. Throughout the operation and what we were just talking about happened before there was combat engagement. But throughout the operation and the advancement of the Kutina special police group, there had been no need for artillery support. I think that the formulation in item 9 was perhaps clumsily made.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Sir, if you had an opportunity to revise it, how would you revise it today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I would stick to the formulation and add an explanation, to the effect that throughout the operation once Crni Vrh was captured, artillery support was not called.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Just a few final questions. Mr. Vurnek, you had said in your testimony this morning that you had a very high regard for Mr. Markac's professionalism. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And I can't recall the -- or I will just summarize the words that you used without quoting you directly, and you can correct me if I'm wrong. You admired his professionalism. And you enjoyed working with him. I don't think that is the precise word that you used. But it was words of -- with that meaning. Can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: That's absolutely true.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: And in your experience, did you always observe him to be a person who upheld and respected the law?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: Everything that I know about him is absolutely positive. He was always respectful of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And would you have also -- or would you also expect him to abide by the rules and the orders of this Court?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN VURNEK
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Well, were you aware that Mr. Markac was provisionally released by this Court?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What does this have to do with anything that happened during and after Operation Storm. I object to the relevance of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. De Landri, the Chamber considers not to be assisted by these questions and the answers to them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE LANDRI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before, Mr. Kuzmanovic, I -- I had the photographs still on my mind. Perhaps it's the easiest way to deal with them right away. Could we have P324 on the screen. And I think it's the third page we would need. It's at least the third paragraph. Witness, is this one of the photographs you were shown when preparing either for your interview or for --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is one of the photographs I saw; it's just that I saw it in black and white.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we see the next photograph. Did you see this one as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw this one as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there is another, a third one, either -- and that would be page 2 or the following page, Mr. Registrar. Yes. Is this -- did you see this photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the other photographs you saw, could we perhaps go to the next one, the ... No, I was not -- I wanted to focus exclusively on the red -- on the red cars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell me, what made you believe that this car was an obstacle and had to be removed from the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I truly don't know what this photograph depicts. However, even today, all vehicles found along the roads abandoned there or elsewhere need to be brought in by the police to the police administrations. After that, an announcement is made that such and such vehicle was found, and the rightful owner is found. Under the law in Croatia, we are duty-bound to bring in such a vehicle, make the announcement, and, if there ever was an owner to show up to claim it, the vehicle is returned. The same regulation was in place in 1995, I believe, as is nowadays. By your leave, Your Honour, I wanted to add that today we had other technical means to move such vehicles at our disposal. In other words, we now have tow-away trucks, which we didn't have during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in all seriousness, are you telling us that, at that time, the concern was to bring cars which were not an obstacle to the traffic to the ordinary police in order to try to find their owners? Is that your testimony? Earlier you had -- you supposed that it had another meaning, it was that the car was without fuel and that it was an obstacle to the track and that is what came to your mind but, although you couldn't -- of course, you couldn't say. But is this now what -- is this now your explanation rather than the previous one, your supposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to repeat, I don't know anything about this specific case. I do suppose, however, that that could have been one of the reasons. I don't know why this vehicle was moved. I truly don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, is it common under those circumstances to put the name of a unit on the car, in order to transfer it to the ordinary police so that they can find the owner? I see the word "Delta" on it. You certainly see that as well. Is that in the context of what you just described so to take care that the car would be returned to their owner would be the normal thing to do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I truly don't know why this was written on the vehicle. I don't know. I simply shared my presumption of what could have been the case involving this vehicle. Finally, up to this day, we never learned who the rightful owner was of this vehicle and what were the circumstances under which it was found at the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You investigated it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know that the rightful owner was never found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was trying to speak about that time, at that moment. I don't know whether the owner was found. And I don't know why that vehicle was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at that time, you apparently knew that, at the time, that the owner was not known. Is that ... because you made a distinction between "later" and "at that time."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know. However, I know of a case when I was transferred to Koprivnica where there was a vehicle within the police administration compound. Once the owner showed up a few months later, the vehicle was returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we look at the next photograph of this same series. What made you believe that this vehicle was without fuel? Or what made you suppose that this vehicle was without fuel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was trying to say that these were merely presumptions. I don't know. One could come up with at least a dozen different explanations as to why that vehicle was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why I'm asking you this question is because your assumptions, which, well, are not directly and immediately supported by the pictures themselves, are fully in line with what other witnesses have told us, and do you have any explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I cannot comment on what other witnesses said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless it has been brought to your attention, or unless it has been discussed with other witnesses. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you say you can't comment on what other witnesses said. Now, first of all, perhaps very factual question: Have you followed the proceedings in this case and ... there's nothing to add to the end. Have you followed the proceedings in this case by Internet or by television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not been following. The only thing was that I read a few articles in the daily press.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the testimony on this vehicle is not -- was totally unknown to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This vehicle says nothing to me. I can only presume what happened with that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that wasn't my question. My question whether you were -- whether you had, through whatever way, become acquainted with what other witnesses said about this car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Thank you for those answers. Mr. Kuzmanovic, I am looking at the clock. We might not be able to finish. I don't know how many questions you have, but -- and I also have a few procedural matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't finish in five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't finish in five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then perhaps it would be better to -- and you would need 15 minutes you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps we should take this first thing in the morning. Would that create any further problems as far as scheduling of this week is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It will not, Your Honour. We have the next witness -- we don't know if the next witness has arrived yet or not, but we are assuming that the witness has, and the witness will be ready to go tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then what else do we have for this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Wednesday we have a hearing, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You will be able to finish that witness tomorrow because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then that's clear, because I just wanted to say -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one second, please. Mr. Vurnek, we have to deal with some procedural matters. We'd like to see you back, it will be very brief tomorrow, but we, unfortunately, can't finish your testimony today. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given or testimony still to be given tomorrow. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please follow Madam Usher, who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a few procedural matters. For the first one, I would like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have to put formally on the record the agreement the parties reached in relation to the timing of calling Witness MM-028. The parties agreed that that witness would be called after the recess and the Chamber has, although not entirely without reluctance, has followed the agreement of the parties, and therefore, we will hear the witness of Witness MM-028 after the recess. Then, finally, since it is a matter of some urgency, the Chamber is seized with a motion for a subpoena for Mr. Brammertz to appear and bring certain materials with him at this Wednesday's hearing. And that would also amount to an expansion of the scope of that hearing. The Gotovina Defence has also asked the Trial Chamber to consider ensuring the appearance of Mr. Bajic at the same hearing. The Chamber denies the motion with reasons to follow, which also means that the scope of the hearing tomorrow [sic] will be limited to its original purpose. The parties would -- yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just as a procedural matter and so the Court has this in mind, I note that the hearing on Wednesday, our agenda is quite full. As I understand it today we have no witness planned for Thursday. So if that's the case, just so that the Court is aware, I don't know if we need Thursday to address what is on the agenda right now for Wednesday, that might be a possibility. But I just wanted to alert the Chamber to that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber still hopes that on Wednesday we can deal with the matters which were originally scheduled for that hearing. And, of course, the Chamber is working hard apart from that on a decision in which the reasons are given for the freeze, to say it. The Chamber does not know exactly at what moment it will have finalized the exact phrasing, the exact language of that decision. That may take some time. It has to be done with full accuracy and precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to make the Chamber aware of the witness after the hearing, his name is Dr. Herman. We are expecting that he will be here Thursday, and be able to presented on Friday. He is a physician, so he had something urgent that he had to attend to. So he will be arriving Thursday and he will be testifying Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are talking about Thursday, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This week, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the witness after tomorrow's witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember his number right now off the top of my head, but ... MM-009. Dr. Ivan Herman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means hearing on Friday, not on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I wanted to make the Chamber aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, thank you for informing us. Because earlier there were some concern as loosing two days at that moment in relation to Witness - what was it - MM-028, I think it was. But one of these days --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were able to have the -- I think it was MM-025 recalled, and the witness, like I said, is arriving today. We thought that witness would be testify last week, so we did some juggling so that we wouldn't loose two court days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's on the record. Thank you. If there is no other matter, we will -- Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just for the record, we received a revised translation of D530, and we are happy with the new translation, so it could be uploaded into the e -- court instead of the old one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the translation which was revised in -- I think on two times the same word used -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Right. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and we have received a memo from CLSS on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are invited to upload it. And, Mr. Registrar, that the translation which is now in e-court be replaced by the new one. I take it that the Prosecution will check carefully whether that is the only changes, but I have no reason to believe that we find anything different other from what is mentioned in the CLSS memo. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 15th of December, 9.00, Courtroom III.
